body:
**Adani–Hindenburg debate**
- SEBI's two final orders dated 18 Sep 2025 held Hindenburg's allegations (incl. concealed related-party transactions via Milestone Tradelinks, Rehvar Infrastructure) "not established", closing proceedings without directions; group stocks rose up to 13% — [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/news/sebi-clears-adani-group-dismisses-hindenburg-allegations-125091801259_1.html); [Moneylife](https://www.moneylife.in/article/adani-group-gets-clean-chit-in-hindenburg-case-sebi-says-no-evidence-of-concealed-related-party-deals/78318.html); [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/sebi-dismisses-hindenburg-researchs-allegations-against-adani-group-494677-2025-09-18)
- SEBI's reasoning was partly that the impugned transactions did not meet the then RPT definition — [Moneylife](https://www.moneylife.in/article/adani-group-gets-clean-chit-in-hindenburg-case-sebi-says-no-evidence-of-concealed-related-party-deals/78318.html)

**SME IPO manipulation and SEBI response**
- SEBI amended ICDR (4 Mar 2025) after finding diversion of IPO proceeds to promoter shells and revenue inflated via circular RPTs; new rules include a minimum operating-profit (EBITDA) eligibility, limits on use of proceeds, minimum application raised from ~₹1 lakh to >₹2 lakh — [The Legal Quorum](https://thelegalquorum.com/reforming-the-sme-ipo-framework-sebis-2025-regulatory-measures/); [IndiaCorpLaw](https://indiacorplaw.in/2025/04/23/strangling-growth-or-ensuring-stability-sebis-new-regulatory-framework-for-smes/); [Agama Law](https://agamalaw.in/2025/05/16/navigating-sme-ipos-recent-regulatory-changes/)
- Enforcement examples: FOCL barred two years (Oct 2025) over fund diversion across ~20 SME IPOs (>₹100 cr); SecUR Credentials (Sep 2025) post-listing coordinated price manipulation — per [Corporate Professionals](https://www.corporateprofessionals.com/?p=11759) (secondary; verify against SEBI orders)
- Oct 2026 SEBI consultation proposes partial recalibration (only unsubscribed portion needs underwriting; align promoter contribution with mainboard) — [Moneylife](https://www.moneylife.in/article/sebi-proposes-sweeping-overhaul-of-sme-ipo-framework/81956.html); [Bar & Bench](https://www.barandbench.com/law-firms/leading-questions/the-sme-ipo-market-in-2026-stricter-entry-smarter-execution)
- NISM overview of SME IPO lacunae — [NISM](https://www.nism.ac.in/blog/lacunae-in-the-sme-ipo-markets)

body:
**Qullamaggie (Kristjan Kullamägi) — three setups**
- Breakout: a stock that already made a big move (e.g., top 1-2% performers over 1/3/6 months), then consolidates in a tightening range ("higher lows," surfing the 10/20-day MAs) for ~2 weeks to 2 months; buy the opening-range high breakout (1-min/5-min ORH) on the daily-chart breakout; stop at the low of the day (stop size should not exceed the stock's ADR, average daily range); sell 1/3-1/2 after 3-5 days, move stop to breakeven, and trail the remainder with the 10- or 20-day MA (close below). Don't anticipate breakouts. — [Tikamalma: Qullamaggie swing trading setups](https://tikamalma.substack.com/p/qullamaggie-swing-trading-setups) [F]; [Retail Traders Repository stream notes](https://retailtradersrepository.substack.com/p/kristjan-kullamagi-qullamaggie-stream-092) [F]
- Episodic Pivot (EP): a news catalyst (earnings blowout, FDA, contract) causing a gap of ~10%+ on very heavy volume, ideally in a stock that has not already run up (neglected); entry on the opening range high; stop at low of the day. In a 2023 stream he reportedly said he now mainly trades EPs. — [Financial Wisdom: Episodic Pivot](https://www.financialwisdomtv.com/post/the-episodic-pivot-strategy-qullamaggie-s-high-momentum-setup-explained) [F]; [Stockbsessed: Episodic pivot](https://stockbsessed.substack.com/p/episodic-pivot-1) [F]
- Parabolic short: stock up several hundred % (large caps ~50-100%+) in days/weeks; short the opening-range low or the first crack/failure at VWAP; targets the 10- and 20-day MAs; higher win rate than his long setups. — [Tikamalma](https://tikamalma.substack.com/p/qullamaggie-swing-trading-setups) [F]; [Stonks Capital: systemizing the parabolic short](https://stonkscapital.substack.com/p/systemizing-kullamagis-parabolic?r=5igdr) [F]
- Risk/expectancy: risk per trade typically 0.25-0.5%, 1% max; win rate only ~25-30% by his own estimate; profits come from rare 10-20R winners. Position size often up to 10-25% of account per position because stops are tight. — [CTE research sheet on Kullamägi](https://completetradersedge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/CTE-Research-Sheet-Kristjan-Kullamagi-market-wizards-next-generation.pdf) [F]
- His claimed growth (roughly $5k to $100M+) is self-reported; a 2026 profile describes a ~$105M figure that "lasted a few days." — [Complete Trader's Edge profile](https://completetradersedge.com/kristjan-kullamagi-qullamaggie/) [F]

body: **Summary:** IT services firms sell people-hours and managed outcomes to global enterprises, with ~55–60% of revenue from the US. They make money on a labour arbitrage: offshore billing rates against Indian salaries, plus pyramid management. Key metrics: constant-currency revenue growth, deal TCV and book-to-bill, attrition, utilisation, EBIT margin, headcount additions, revenue per employee, top-client concentration and vertical mix (BFSI, retail, manufacturing). Cycle drivers: US/EU IT budgets and discretionary spend, BFSI health, the USD/INR rate (a weaker rupee adds ~30–40 bps of margin per 1% depreciation), technology shifts (cloud in 2020–22; GenAI deflating application services in 2025–26) and H-1B and visa policy. Lead indicators: Accenture quarterly bookings, Gartner IT spending forecasts, US non-farm IT employment, Naukri JobSpeak, hyperscaler capex, deal announcements. Winners rode each new wave early (TCS and Infosys with Y2K and offshoring; Persistent and Coforge with digital in 2020–24), kept strong client mining and protected margins. Losers clung to a legacy mix (Wipro's 2015–23 stagnation, Mphasis's HP-channel decline) or made acquisition-led pivots that diluted margins. Valuation: P/E roughly 15–20x in 2013–19 and ~30–35x at the Dec 2021 peak. Nifty IT was ~18x in Jun 2026 against a 27x 7-year median. Nov 2026: Infosys grew only +1.5% CC YoY in Q2 FY27 and cut FY27 guidance to 1–2%, even though large-deal TCV was $5.2 bn and AI revenue grew 29% QoQ. Traps: TCV that does not convert, and rupee-led growth. Sources: [1](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/infosys-q2-revenue-edges-up-but-trims-full-year-revenue-outlook) · [2](https://ticker.finology.in/discover/market-update/infosys-q2-fy27-results-analysis) · [3](https://www.bajajbroking.in/share-market-news/it-q2-fy27-preview-tcs-infosys-growth-seen-as-muted) · [4](https://www.indexpe.in/blog/nifty-sector-valuations-june-2026) Links: about `insight:twin-engine`
title: sector_playbooks › Sector playbook: Indian IT services

body:
- **Valuation timing matters.** Since 2004, every negative 5-year Nifty return started at P/E ≥ 24.5;
  starting below P/E 12 gave ~29%/yr.
- **Indian winners mostly grew profits;** only ~37% of the median gain came from a higher P/E. Stocks
  that ended their run at P/E 70+ are mostly lower today (median −48%).
- **Small caps fall >20% about every 2 years** and spent 36% of days (2004–26) >30% below their peak.
- **Tone isn't an edge in India** — optimistic concall language moves prices short-term but doesn't
  predict results. Checking promises vs delivery is the edge.
- **Never trust a company's own "no pledge" statement** — check the exchange data.

body:
We read 10 earnings calls each for Uniparts and Skipper and checked every promise against what happened.
- **Uniparts:** credibility +0.28. Numbers guidance reliable under the new CEO (78% hit), but execution
  promises keep slipping (Mexico plant ~10 months late, promised acquisition never happened). Stays 72/100.
- **Skipper:** only ~41% of promises delivered; capacity date moved 5 times; promised "no more equity"
  then raised ₹433.5 cr. **Downgraded from buy-zone to watchlist (66 → 55).**
- New rule: no stock goes in the buy zone without this credibility check.

Also added: governance history of **43 Indian business groups** (clean → severe), **29 lessons straight
from Buffett's letters and Howard Marks' memos**, and **Indian base rates** (about half of IPOs trade below
issue price; ~3 in 4 active funds lag the index over 10 years; momentum and value factors have worked in
India, small size by itself has not).

body:
Phases, in order (each partial, overlapping, never "finished"):
1. **C — Learn continuously. Never stop.** Knowledge, cases, methods, data — India AND US.
2. **Teach ourselves:** practise analysing and stock picking until measurably good (blind drills,
   calibration, forward paper calls). "Before teaching me, teach yourself."
3. **A — Build the thinking system** that can teach the user.
4. **B — Research partner:** bring specific ideas only once the edge is *proven* (see gate in curriculum.md).
Rules: hypothesis-testing on stocks is fine, but never a stock-picking session; work with intention to
become the best. If a genuinely great stock turns up, mention it. Capital and the user's job don't matter.
"We grow or we lose together. Don't rest. Keep working. Have the grit." Claude = the user's sleeper cell.

- Twin engine: multibaggers = EPS growth × P/E rerating (Radico ≈ 7.5x × 5x ≈ 38x).
- Expect deep drawdowns in winners (Amazon −94%, NVIDIA >50% twice, Radico −74% in 2008).
- Size so being wrong is survivable; a few winners pay for many losers.
- Disqualifiers regardless of price: promoter pledge, qualified audit, margin jump with
  no identifiable cause, debt-funded growth with negative CFO.

body:
We read 10 earnings calls each for Uniparts and Skipper and checked every promise against what happened.
- **Uniparts:** credibility +0.28. Numbers guidance reliable under the new CEO (78% hit), but execution
  promises keep slipping (Mexico plant ~10 months late, promised acquisition never happened). Stays 72/100.
- **Skipper:** only ~41% of promises delivered; capacity date moved 5 times; promised "no more equity"
  then raised ₹433.5 cr. **Downgraded from buy-zone to watchlist (66 → 55).**
- New rule: no stock goes in the buy zone without this credibility check.

Also added: governance history of **43 Indian business groups** (clean → severe), **29 lessons straight
from Buffett's letters and Howard Marks' memos**, and **Indian base rates** (about half of IPOs trade below
issue price; ~3 in 4 active funds lag the index over 10 years; momentum and value factors have worked in
India, small size by itself has not).
